pairs.subject: realtime-events
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/webhook.rs:262 Webhook publication accepts arbitrary event names independently of payload types, allowing vocabulary and payload contracts to drift.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/events.rs:139 SSE uses internal broadcast receivers; this capacity bounds buffered messages, not provider topics or account connections, and searches found no provider subscription-cap mechanism.

crates/server/src/worker.rs:1562 Watch capture reads committed revisions through one unpaged query capped at 1,000 rows per app; excess changes receive neither overflow accounting nor a coarse invalidation.

crates/server/src/worker.rs:1938 Within the captured batch, watches receive revisions together per app/dataset without merging distinct occurrences; Slack summarizes the batch with its revision count.
crates/server/src/webhook.rs:263 The publication door accepts an arbitrary name and independently serializable payload rather than a registry-bound event variant; producers supply literal names.

crates/server/src/webhook.rs:592 When persistence fails, delivery proceeds with a generated ID and no durable retry row; initial deliveries are also scheduled before their rows are created, leaving a crash-loss window despite the implemented retry ladder and DLQ.

crates/server/src/routes/events.rs:86 SSE streams own their broadcast receivers, subscribe before asynchronous snapshots, and terminate on shutdown; dropping the stream releases its receiver without an outstanding asynchronous subscription handshake.
